# Itiha intelligence brief, 2026-11-21

**The Tipu Short is a day overdue and the Guru Tegh Bahadur Short, due 24 November, has no script either: script Tegh Bahadur today. The Indonesia long-form is past day three with 71,382 views, and its first subscribers run at 3.4 per 1,000 against 2 for the Asia one, so the Bali follow-up stays.**

## This week: 3 decisions
1. **Script and publish a Short on Aurangzeb's order to execute Guru Tegh Bahadur, for 24 November.** (short, due 2026-11-24, open since 2026-11-15)  
   Why: Three days out, the top date on the radar, and it names Aurangzeb, the villain of the channel's two largest videos. Breakouts are the lever furthest behind: 0 subscribers from them this month against 1,554 planned. It rests on the date and the name: Mughal Shorts with no film behind them have landed below the usual.  
   First step: Script it today. Open on Gurdwara Sis Ganj in Chandni Chowk, then Aurangzeb's order: an act of state, not a martyrdom story. Title starts “Guru Tegh Bahadur”. Record on 22, publish 23 November at 17:00 IST.
2. **Script, record and publish one Tipu Sultan Short on the fall of Srirangapatna in 1799: who took the treasure, and who wrote his story afterwards.** (short, due 2026-11-20, open since 2026-11-15)  
   Why: Overdue since 20 November, still no script on disk, and it lapses by itself on 23 November. The case for it is unchanged: the owner's pick of 15 November, and the Tipu Jayanti row has been in the news for three days. But its date has passed and Tegh Bahadur's has not, so it comes second.  
   First step: Decide today. If both Shorts can be scripted this weekend, write this one straight after Tegh Bahadur and publish it by 22 November. If not, press Drop on the Today tab so the list stays honest.
3. **Script and publish a follow-up long-form for the Indonesia video's viewers: why Bali stayed Hindu when Java converted.** (long, due 2026-12-02, open since 2026-11-19)  
   Why: The Indonesia long-form has 71,382 views and is one of three videos this month to cross the channel's top-hit line. Its first subscribers run at 3.4 per 1,000 views against 2 for the Asia one. Follow it while viewers still arrive. The topic is a guess from its Indonesian comments.  
   First step: On 22 November, if the Indonesia rate is still above the Asia one's, start the source list on Majapahit's fall and the priests who moved to Bali. Write it after the Tegh Bahadur Short is out.

Everything below is the evidence. Mark a decision done or dropped on the Brief tab; an open one stays here until then.

## Channel health
18,000 subscribers against 100,000 by 28 September 2027. November's milestone is 19,934, which needs 69.6 net a day; the 7-day rate is 102.6 and the 28-day rate 49.7. Projection basis: 28-day rate; the 7-day rate is a spike, so the week's jump is not carried forward: the month ends at 18,447, 1,487 short, and the channel is 1,261 behind the ramp today. Only 46.3% of net subscribers over 28 days came from videos; the rest is tied to no video and can stop without warning. The lever furthest behind is breakouts, 0 against 1,554 this month; one video of that size closes the month. Last week (9 to 15 November) five Shorts shipped and none came from this list: the two Ravana film Shorts beat the usual and the two after them fell below it, which is why this week's Shorts are dated moments, not the film. Long-form's subscribers per 1,000 views over the 365-day window have fallen out of their usual range, to 7.7.

What's working
- “How the Ramayana Was REWRITTEN to Convert Hindus” is the month's long-form: 71,382 views in 89 hours, 801.5 an hour against 301 for the Asia long-form over its life, a like rate of 1.8% against 0.9%, and viewers writing “Great video, subscribed!” under it.
- Long-form still brings most of what uploads bring: 79.2% of upload net subscribers over 28 days (511 against 134 from Shorts), on 44.4% of upload views.
- The best converter in the 90-day window is “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History”, at 13.3 net subscribers per 1,000 views. Its lesson is the Tegh Bahadur Short's shape: “Name the villain, convict him with a document or payment he cannot deny, then end on who is still repeating him today.” Here that means who gave the order and what the record says, checked before recording.

What's wrong
- Neither dated Short has a script on disk: Tipu was due on 20 November and Tegh Bahadur's script was due today. Probable cause: the owner's own picks fill the week (the Sonia Gandhi Short on 20 November, the Param Vir Chakra script the same day, the ICS salaries Short reopened on 19 November). Test: none, it is a choice. Script Tegh Bahadur first, because its date will not move.
- Reach is not turning into subscribers at the old rate: the Indonesia long-form 3.4 per 1,000 views and the Asia one 2, against 8.3 for long-form over the channel's life. Probable cause: Home-feed plays that are not real viewing. 195,639 long-form views over 28 days came from the Home and subscriptions bucket against 5,572 from search, and only 41.4% of November's long-form views were engaged views. Test: the Indonesia video has no transcript in the script library, so the check of where its viewers left could not run; add it (see housekeeping) before writing the Bali script.
- Shorts views fell 58.0% week over week to 2026-11-18. Probable cause: the Ravana film Shorts' run of 11 November left the window and nothing dated replaced it; the later film Shorts, “Every Ramayana Kept One Rule” (1,703 views) and “Why Is Lord Rama in the Original Constitution of India?” (1,392), stayed below the usual. Search no longer carries Shorts either: it brought 30.1% of Shorts views over 28 days, out of its usual range. Test: the Tegh Bahadur Short's first three days.

## Audience
Analytics runs to 2026-11-18, the Indonesia long-form's second day. Long-form is watched from the Home feed: 195,639 long-form views over 28 days came from the bucket that holds Home and the subscriptions feed, against 5,572 from search. Engaged views were 40.5% of long-form views over 90 days, so a view counts for less than it did before August.
- Most new subscribers click on the channel page, not under a video: 976 subscribers gained over 28 days carried no video, against 645 net from all uploads. Community posts brought 2 on 394,711 views; they buy views, not subscribers.
- The Indonesia long-form found Indonesia: viewers from Java and the wider archipelago answer it, correct it and add to it, and Indian viewers say they subscribed because of it. Nobody has tested that audience with a second video yet; the Bali follow-up is the test.
- Shorts now live on the Shorts feed: 158,756 Shorts views over 28 days came from it, against 79,922 from search. A searched name in the title still matters for the long tail, which is why the Tegh Bahadur title starts with his name.
- WhatsApp is the outside source that sends viewers: 12,586 views over the 365-day window against Instagram's 458. The most forwarded long-forms are the temple tax and Goa ones.

## How they are reacting
The Indonesia long-form holds most of the week's comments: anger at the rewrite, Indonesians answering from Java, and new subscribers saying why they subscribed. Under the Asia long-form the most-liked objection is still the Chola one. The Sai Pallavi Short still draws the row.
- **Anger at the rewrite** (negative): "So, Fanfiction trying to make themselves canon."
- **Subscribing because of it** (positive): "Now I know it all started with Parameswara wanting successful trade. Great video, subscribed!"
- **Indonesians answering back** (positive): "Hello from Indonesia! Watching this hit close to home because we are living through the exact implications of what you just explained."
- **A correction from Indonesia** (mixed): "Rama were never worshiped in Classical Nusantara (present day countries describe as malay archipelago) esp. in the Majapahit era"
- **The Chola objection** (mixed): "“Never sent a single soldier…” ever heard of Chola Empire?"
- **The Sai Pallavi row, still going** (negative): "Playing Maa Sita and saying that statement is contradictory. She didn't feel the pain of maa Sita when playing the role"

Requested topics
- Rajendra Chola's fleet to Srivijaya, the most-liked objection under the Asia long-form
- Hindi versions of the long-forms, asked again under the Indonesia one
- A Krishna video in the shape of the Asia Ramayana one
- Bagan in Myanmar
- The Hindu titles Thai kings took (Devaraja, Dharmaraja)

## Competitors
The watchlist is still mostly the Ramayana film and the boycott row around it. Two openings are worth borrowing this week, one for each video in the decisions.
- **Project SHIVOHAM**: "She's NOT Subhadra? The Forgotten Ancient Goddess"
  Why it worked: 261,663 views at 10x the channel's median, a long-form. It opens on a place everyone knows (“At Puri Jagannath, millions worship…”), asks a question everyone thinks they can answer, gives the expected answer, then turns it: “But what if the answer is not so simple?”
  Steal: The opening for the Bali long-form: the Bali temple every Indian tourist has seen, the answer everyone gives for why the island is Hindu, then the part they do not know.
- **The Emissary**: "Why Did Japan Make Indian Propaganda Posters?"
  Why it worked: 588,807 views at 16.3x the channel's median, a Short. It opens on the object (“Check out these posters from India's freedom struggle. Japan made them.”) and asks why in the third sentence.
  Steal: Open the Tegh Bahadur Short the same way: the gurdwara the viewer can picture first, then the order that put it there.

Gaps
- Aurangzeb as a long-form: Mohak Mangal's “Reality of Aurangzeb” is still unanswered by every tracked channel and by Itiha. If the Tegh Bahadur Short lands, that is the long-form it points to.
- Caste among India's Muslims: Mohak Mangal's “Reality of CASTEISM in Muslims” has no answer from a tracked channel or from Itiha (see ideas).

## Trending now, make this
- **today, short, 3/5**: Tipu Sultan: a day overdue, no script  
  Signal: Due on 20 November, the calendar's date for him. The Tipu Jayanti row (News18 Marathi) has been in the news for three days. (Decision, news)  
  Make: Script it straight after Tegh Bahadur and publish by 22 November, or press Drop on the Today tab. It lapses on 23 November.
- **today, short, 3/5**: The Malay Ramayana Short: already cut, not on YouTube  
  Signal: The Short on Ravana getting his powers from Allah has been on Instagram since 20 November but not on YouTube. Its script was written to send viewers to the Indonesia long-form, which runs at 801.5 views an hour. (Script on disk, own long-form)  
  Make: Upload it as a YouTube Short today or tomorrow, title starting with “Ravana”, with the Indonesia long-form as its related video, and keep 23 November clear for Tegh Bahadur. That it sends viewers to the long-form is a guess.
- **this_week, short, 3/5**: Guru Tegh Bahadur, 24 November  
  Signal: The top date on the radar, three days out. The radar's step this week is to record and cut the Short, titled with the searched name “guru tegh bahadur history”. The calendar flags the martyrdom framing as one to avoid. (Moments radar, calendar)  
  Make: Script today, record on 22 November, publish on 23 November at about 17:00 IST. Judge it on day three, 26 November, and on search over the year, by the channel's own lesson: “Persecution memory with a named defender, released on its anniversary, earns search traffic for a year; judge it on lifetime search views, not on day-three feed widening.”
- **this_week, short, 3/5**: Winston Churchill's birth anniversary, 30 November  
  Signal: Nine days out. The radar's step this week is to research him with named sources and script a Short on the colonial mechanism: who ordered it, who profited, what the British record itself admits. (Moments radar)  
  Make: Only if a slot opens after Tegh Bahadur: one Short on the Bengal famine of 1943, convicted from British papers (the War Cabinet record, Leo Amery's diary), checked before recording, published on 30 November. The channel's earlier Churchill Short failed on this lesson: “The one-sentence context rule applies inside the first 10 seconds most of all.”
- **watch, skip, 1/5**: Tarabai imprisons Rajaram II, 24 November 1750  
  Signal: On the radar for the same date as Tegh Bahadur (from an on-this-day list), and the Tarabai Short is one of the channel's four breakouts. (Moments radar)  
  Make: Skip. Two Shorts on one date split one sitting, and Tegh Bahadur has the bigger searched name. The breakout set Tarabai against Aurangzeb; this is a Maratha court quarrel with no outside villain.
- **watch, skip, 2/5**: Rajiv and Indira Gandhi on Wikipedia  
  Signal: English readership of Rajiv Gandhi at 3.19x its 30-day median and Indira Gandhi at 2.22x, with the Emergency and Indira Gandhi in the news all week. (Wikipedia pageviews, news)  
  Make: Skip until the Sonia Gandhi Short has its day three on 23 November (655 views so far). Shorts on recent politics have landed below the usual here, so another would rest on the spike alone.

## Topic ideas (voltage-checked)
- [2/5, short] **Did India Ever Send an Army to Southeast Asia? The Chola Raid on Srivijaya**  
  Contested history: it answers the most-liked objection to the Asia long-form's “never sent a single soldier”; Empire mechanism: a raid on the kingdom that held the straits and their trade  
  source: Comments under “Why Does All of Asia Know the Ramayana?”. A guess from comments, not a result; it also lets the channel correct its own video in public.
- [3/5, long] **The Castes the British Census Found Among India's Muslims**  
  Identity, caste and religion stakes; Empire mechanism: the census that sorted Indians into ranked groups; Hidden history: caste is usually told as a Hindu story only  
  source: Open in the counter-channel list: Mohak Mangal's “Reality of CASTEISM in Muslims” has no answer from a tracked channel or Itiha. The nearest on the channel is the Halley Kalyan caste long-form. Rests on that open demand, not on a test of this topic here.

## Instagram (separate platform, separate audience)
Instagram has 25,540 followers, up 247 in 7 days, 35.3 a day. The Sonia Gandhi reel reached 2,871 with a 54.2% skip rate, too new to judge. Carousels remain the growth format at 3.71x the median reach of reels.

Do more
- Build every carousel at 7-10 cards  
  The median carousel in the 7-10 band converts 36 followers (89 posts); outside the band, 12 (15 posts). Pooled rate 2.97 vs 1.88 follows per 1k reach — the band is not just reaching more people, it converts better per person reached, so this is not a reach artefact. 399 followers a month at stake.
- Write carousels in the revision lane  
  50 revision carousels in the band converted a median 53.5 followers against 22 for the other lanes (39 posts). Median reach 15.9k vs 12.5k, conversion 3.77 vs 2.12 per 1k. 383 followers a month at stake.

Do less
- Stop making posts that get shared without bringing followers  
  19 of 102 rated posts are shared above the median (25.4/1k) but convert below it (2.2/1k): median 12.8k reach for a median 12 followers. The 32 posts that do both average 290 followers each. Share rate and follow rate correlate at only 0.39 — shareable and followable are separate skills, and the first one flatters itself on the home screen. 1,005 followers a month at stake.
- Stop posting single images  
  87 single images all time: 83.7k reach between them and 119 followers, 1.4 per post. A carousel in the 7-10 band averages 159.6. Every image slot is a carousel slot not taken. 94 followers a month at stake.

## Housekeeping
- **now**: Reply under the Majapahit correction on “How the Ramayana Was REWRITTEN to Convert Hindus”: what Majapahit's court worshipped, and that the Adam-and-Allah version is the Malay Hikayat Seri Rama. Keep the current pinned comment. /replies drafts it.  
  The video is still climbing, so every new viewer reads its top comments, and the correction is among the most liked. That a reply helps is a guess.
- **this_week**: Put the Indonesia long-form's final script or transcript in the long-form scripts folder so the next refresh can show where its viewers left.  
  Its drop-off check could not run without it, and the Bali script should be written knowing where this one lost people.
- **this_week**: If not done yet, put the Indonesia long-form on the end screen of “Why Does All of Asia Know the Ramayana?”.  
  The Asia long-form has 159,865 views on the same subject. The Indonesia video's pinned comment links back to it, but the Asia one's pinned comment shows no link the other way. That it helps is a guess.
- **this_week**: If not done yet, check in Studio why “How Jati's evolve organically ?” has 2 views since 3 November.  
  A public Short gets at least a handful of views, so none at all points to its visibility setting or a restriction, not the topic.
- **later**: Ask the designer for a second thumbnail for “The Church That Ran Britain's PRISON Camps” and run a Test & Compare in Studio.  
  It is the best converter over the 365-day window: 34.2 subscribers per 1,000 views on only 1,082 views: the people who find it subscribe, too few find it.
